senses: to defend, guard or protect, to stand up for, to stick up for
la:verb:defendo.html:
dē-fendo, di, sum (
infin. pass. parag.: defendier, : .— Part. gen. plur. sync.: defendentum,), 3, v. a.
arch.: FENDO; cf. Sanscr. han (ghan), to smite; Gr. θείνω; hence, also offendo, infensus, infestus, mani-festus; cf. fustis
, to fend or ward off any thing hostile or injurious; to repel, avert, keep off: propulsando arcere (for syn. cf.: tueor, tutor, servo, conservo. propugno, protego, vindico, caveo—freq. and class.); regularly constr. with acc. alone (so in Cic. and Caes.); very rarely aliquid (aliquem) ab aliquo, and in poets also aliquid alicui; cf. Zumpt. Gr. § 469.
Aliquid (aliquem): ut tu morbos calamitates intemperiasque prohibessis, defendas averruncesque,: serva cives, defende hostes, cum potes defendere, Enn. ap. ; cf. bellum (opp. inferre),; fin.: ad defendendos ictus ac repellendos,; cf.: ignis jactus et lapides,: frigus et solem,; cf.: nimios solis ardores,; and frigus,; also: sitim fonte et purā lymphā,to quench,: qui non defendit injuriam neque propulsat,; so, injuriam,: noxiam,: imperatoris sui tribunorumque plebis injurias,: vim suorum,; cf.: vim illatam vi,: pericula,; : hunc furorem,: dedecus manu, et saep.: crimen,to answer, defend against an accusation,.—
With ab: (milites) a pinnis hostes defendebant facillime, Quadrig. ap. ; cf. : hostem a fossa,: ignem a tectis,.—
Aliquid alicui (cf. arceo, no. II. d.): iniuriam foribus,: solstitium pecori,; cf.: aestatem capellis,; : tela misero,: dedecus morti,: senium famae,.—
Absol., to put a stop (to a fire), to check the flames: nec quisquam defendere audebat, crebris minis restinguere prohibentium,; cf.: urbem incendere, feris in populum immissis, quo difficilius defenderentur,.—
Transf., like prohibere, with acc. of that from which any thing is warded off or averted, to defend, guard, protect, cover.
In gen. (so most freq. in all perr. and species of composition), constr. with acc. alone; with acc. and ab aliquo (contra aliquid), or merely ab aliquo; and absol.
With simple acc.: Aeduos ceterosque amicos populi Rom.,: eos,; : se armis,: se manu,; 6, 40, 6 et saep.: castra,fin.; ; (with tueri): oppidum, et saep.: eum defendo, quem tu accusas,: aliquem apud praetores,: aliquem de ambitu,: cf. causam,; ; et passim: d. ac tegere scelus,; cf. with protegere,: justitiam,: communem salutem,; et saep.: locum,to preserve, maintain,; cf.: vicem modo rhetoris atque poëtae,to sustain,: actorum partes,: aedes Vestae vix defensa est (sc. ab incendio),preserved,.—
Aliquid (aliquem) ab aliquo: Aedui cum se suaque ab iis defendere non possent,: se a finitimis,; ; et saep.: Galliam omnem ab Ariovisti injuria,; so, aliquem ab injuria,; ; cf. : se regnumque suum ab Romanorum avaritia,: provinciam non modo a calamitate, sed etiam a metu calamitatis,: Italiam a vastatione, Planc. ap. : vitam ab inimicorum audacia telisque,: libertatis causam ab regio praesidio, et saep.: teneras myrtos a frigore,: frondes ab acutae vulnere falcis, a pecoris morsu, et saep.—
With ab aliquo: quod et ab incendio lapis et ab ariete materia defendit,; so ; .—
Aliquem (aliquid) contra, or adversus aliquem: me scio a te contra iniquos meos solere defendi,: sese adversus populum Romanum defendere,: me adversus Abrupolim,; ; ; : auctoritatem contra invidiam,; ; ; ; ; ; .—(ε) Absol.: filii qui et sentire et defendere possent,: cum jam defenderet nemo,: defendentibus civibus Romanis,; cf. in the abl. absol., ; ; et saep.: quibus eae partes ad defendendum obvenerunt, —
In partic.
Of speech, to defend, support, maintain; to bring forward, allege in defence (so repeatedly in Cic.; elsewhere rare).
With acc.: (Carneades) nullam umquam in illis suis disputationibus rem defendit, quam non probarit,; cf. : me id maxime defendisse, ut, etc.,have chiefly striven for,; ; .—
With acc. and inf.: gravissimeque et verissime defenditur, numquam aequitatem ab utilitate posse sejungi, etc.,; ; : ille nihil ex his sponte susceptum sed principi paruisse defendebat,: sed id solitum esse fieri defendebat,; so with verb pass. and inf., —
With a relative clause: (quae turpitudines) cur non cadant in sapientem, non est facile defendere,. —
In the later jurid. Lat., to claim, vindicate, or prosecute at law: quia libertatem et hereditatem ex testamento sibi defendebat,: si patris mortem defendere necesse habuerit,i. e. legally to avenge his death,; .

la:verb:defendendus.gloss: which is to be driven away
senses: which is to be driven away
which is to be defended, which is to be guarded, which is to be protected

la:noun:deformitas.gloss: The state of being deformed; deformity, ugliness, disfigurement.
senses: The state of being deformed; deformity, ugliness, disfigurement.
The state of being morally incorrect; baseness, vileness, appalling nature; disgrace.
la:noun:deformitas.html:
dēformĭtas, ātis, f.
deformis, no. I.
,
deformity, ugliness (good prose).
Lit. (physically): quae si in deformitate corporis habet aliquid offensionis, quanta illa depravatio et foeditas animi debet videri?; ; cf. of mutilation, : in tanta deformitate,hideousness,; : aedificiorum,.—
Trop. (morally), baseness, vileness, deformity of character: an corporis pravitates habebunt aliquid offensionis, animi deformitas non habebit?; ; ; ; ; .—Plur.: verba meretricum vitia atque deformitates significantia, et saep.—
An uncouth style: rusticitas et rigor et deformitas adferunt frigus,.

la:verb:defero.gloss: to bear, carry or bring down or away; convey; take, remove
senses: to bear, carry or bring down or away; convey; take, remove
to give to someone, grant, confer upon, allot, offer to someone, bestow
to bring or give an account of, deliver or bear news or information, report, announce, state
to report someone's name before the praetor, as plaintiff or informer; indict, impeach, denounce, accuse
la:verb:defero.html:
dē-fĕro, tŭli, lātum, ferre,
v. a., to bear or bring away a thing from a place; to bear, carry, bring down.
Lit.
In gen.
Without stating the terminus (not very freq.): roseam Auroram per oras Aetheris,; ; : Rhodanus amnis segnem deferens Ararim,; ; ; ex Helicone coronam,: ramalia arida tecto,. —Absol.: flumina liquida ac deferentia,—Far more freq.,
Indicating the terminus (by ad, in, an adv. of place, the dat., etc.): literas ad Caesarem,: epistolam ad Ciceronem, and 8; cf.: mandata ad aliquem,; : aurum ad gnatum suum,; cf. ; ; natos ad flumina,: Germani ad castra Romanorum delati, et saep.: semen quod ex arbore per surculos defertur in terram,: aurum et omnia ornamenta sua in aerarium,: aedes in planum et colli subicere,: cf. : ferrum in pectus,: castra in viam,: aciem in campos,: in praeceps deferri,; cf. ; : praeceps in undas deferar,; : in vicum, et saep.: hunc sub aequora,i. e. submerge,: quasdam (virgines) ex plebe homines domos deferebant,: si forte eo (sc. Demetriadem) deferret fuga regem,: quo pennis delata sit ales,: cum pallam mihi Detulisti,; so, epistolas alicui, et saep.
In partic.
Naut. t. t., to drive away, drive down, drive a ship, or those on board a ship, to any place: onerariae duae paullo infra delatae sunt,; : una (navis) delata Oricum,: (Labienus) longius delatus aestu, etc.,: quem cum ex alto ignotas ad terras tempestas et in desertum litus detulisset,; cf. .—
Rarely in gen., to bring, convey to any place (as a ship, its passengers): e portu navis huc nos dormientes detulit,.—
Mercant. t. t., to bring to market, to sell (post-Aug.): nexos maniplos,: pallium. : videamus hoc, quod concupiscimus, quanti deferatur,.
Trop.
In gen., to bring: redde harmoniaī Nomen, ab organicis alto delatum Heliconi,brought,; : (Alexander) eadem fortunae pignora in discrimen detulisset,; cf.: fabulas in certamen,: hac re ad consilium delata, having been takeninto consideration, ; so, rem ad consilium,: qui ad agendum nihil cogitati detulerit,: (poëta) si foret hoc nostrum delatus in aevum, Detereret sibi multa,. —
With particular accessory notions.
To bring, give to one, grant, confer upon, allot, to offer to any one, transfer, deliver (for syn. v. do—very freq.).
Aliquid ad aliquem: ad hunc totius belli summam omnium voluntate deferri,: imperium ad aliquem,; 7, 4, 6; ; : omnem rem ad Pompeium,; cf.: omnia ad unum,: causam ad Galbam,: primas ad aliquem, et saep.—
Aliquid alicui: sibi a Caesare regnum civitatis deferri,; Fasti ap. ; cf.: regnum et diadema uni,: fasces indigno,: praemium dignitatis alicui (opp. denegare),: ultro ei legationem (opp. denegare),; cf. : palmam alicujus rei Crasso,; cf. ; : omnem ei auctoritatem,: pacem hostibus,: Octaviam neptem condicionem, et saep. —
With acc. alone, or absol.: jusjurandum,to tender an oath,; cf. ib. § 3 and § 4; si quid petet, ultro defer, et saep.—
To bring or give an account of, to report, announce, signify, state (for syn. v. declaro init.— very freq.): qui nostra consilia ad adversarios deferat,; so, aliquid ad aliquem,; ; ; et saep.: ut (haec) per eos ad Caesarem deferrentur,fin.; so with per, ; : qui ad Caesarem detulerint delaturive sint, me poenitere consilii mei,; so with acc. and inf., ; —
Legal t. t.: nomen, and post-Aug., aliquem, to indict, impeach, accuse before the pretor, as plaintiff or informer (for syn. cf.: denuntio, indico): nomen alicujus de parricidio,: nomen amici mei de ambitu,; ; nomen suo familiari (dat.) eadem de re, : nomen tibi,; cf.: illi nonnihil tamen in deferendo nomine secuti,: ad deferendos reos praemio duci,: reos ad praetorem,: reos ejusdem criminis detulerunt,; cf.: defertur majestatis, (v. Draeger ad loc.): adulterii,: impietatis in principem,: Drusus defertur moliri res novas,; cf.: defertur simulavisse partum,: ad deferenda de Perseo crimina,; cf. ; cf. also: et cum occiderentur, detuli sententiam,voted to condemn,. —Absol.: et minari et deferre etiam non orator potest,.—Of denouncing: quae apud vos de me deferunt,.—
Pub. law t. t.
Aliquid ad aerarium, and more freq. simply aliquid, to give in at the Aerarium: horum nomina ad aerarium detulisset,: quamquam rationes deferre properarim (for which referre is repeatedly used just before),.—Hence of persons, to recommend them for future consideration and reward, for their services to the state: in beneficiis ad aerarium delatus est,; ; ; : senatus consultum factum ad aerarium deferre,the public archives,; ; ; .—
Deferre in censum, to report any thing for assessment, to return one's property to the censors: mille quingentum aeris in censum,; for which, deferre censum,; .—Pass. in mid. force: deferri in censum,to report one's self for assessment,.—
To ascribe, .

la:verb:defenso.html:
dēfenso, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a. intens. [defendo]. *
To fend off diligently, ward off: metus,.—
To defend diligently, protect (rare; mostly ante-class. and poet., not in Cic. or Caes.): moenia,; ; : alios ab hostibus,: humeros,: se ipsa moenia, (al. defendebant): se injuria,.—Absol.: dum defensamus (sc. armentum),.

la:verb:definio.gloss: to bound, set bounds to; to limit
senses: to bound, set bounds to; to limit
to define, explain, designate by limiting
la:verb:definio.html:
dēfīnĭo, īvi, ītum, 4, v. a.
To bound, to set bounds to; to limit, terminate, define (for syn. v. decerno—freq. in Cic.).
Lit.: ejus fundi extremam partem oleae directo ordine definiunt,; cf. : orbes caeli aspectum nostrum definiunt,; cf. : orbem terrarum (loca),; imperium populi R., —
Trop.
To designate by limiting; to limit, define, determine; to explain (cf. circumscribo, no. II. A.): genus universum brevi circumscribi et definiri potest,; cf. : universam et propriam oratoris vim,: definienda res erit verbis et breviter describenda,; cf. ; fin.: omitto innumerabiles viros, etc.... unum hoc definio, tantam esse necessitatem virtutis, etc., this only I declare, etc., fin.: probe definitur a Stoicis fortitudo, cum eam virtutem esse dicunt propugnantem pro aequitate, ; ; et saep.: nec uno modo definitur res eadem,; et saep.: aedes sibi optimas, hortos, etc.,; cf.: ut suus cuique locus erat definitus,: tempus adeundi,: cf.: ante quem diem iturus sit,: annos,: consulatum in annos,; cf.: potestatem in quinquennium,: ut quam vitam ingrediar, definias,; cf. : non remittam: definitum est,it is determined, decided,; ; .—
In opposition to breadth or laxity (cf. circumscribo, no. II. 2), to limit within certain bounds, to restrict, confine: non vagabitur oratio mea longius atque eis fere ipsis definietur viris, qui, etc.,: quae sententia definit amicitiam paribus officiis ac voluntatibus,; cf. : ex perduellium numero definitus, included in the definition of, Off. 3, 29, 107 (dub.). —
To terminate, finish (very rare; perh. only in the foll. places): ut totam hujus generis orationem concludam atque definiam, Zumpt; : definito juvene, ended, i. e. slain, Apul. M. 8, p. 203, 20.—Hence, dēfīnītus, a, um, P. a. (according to no. I. B. 1), definite, limited, distinct, precise; plain, perspicuous (rare, but good prose): quaestionum duo sunt genera: alterum infinitum, alterum definitum. Definitum est, quod ὑπόθεσιν Graeci, nos causam, etc., ; so opp. generales,: certum esse in caelo ac definitum locum, ubi, etc.,; so with certus,; : quaestiones,fin.—Adv.: dē-fīnītē, definitely, precisely, distinctly,

etc., ; de Or. 2, 27, 118; ; —Comp. and sup. do not occur.

la:noun:defensio.html:
dēfensĭo, ōnis, f.
defendo, no. II.
,
a defending, defence.
Prop.: Remis cum spe defensionis studium propugnandi accessit,.—With gen. subj.: urbium,; : ad istam omnem orationem brevis est defensio,; ; : nostra propugnatio ac defensio dignitatis tuae, et saep.— With gen. obj.: defensio criminis,: criminum,: sceleris,.—
Concr., a written defence, speech: defensionem Demosthenes legit,.—
As jurid. t. t.
The legal maintenance of a right: libertatis,.—
(Acc. to defendo, no. II. B. 2.) Legal prosecution, punishment of a crime: mortis,.

la:noun:defensor.html:
dēfensor, ōris, m., rar. f.
id.
.
One who fends, wards, averts, or keeps off: necis,: periculi,.—
A defender, protector.
In gen. (for syn. cf.: tutor, praeses, vindex, cognitor, curator, patronus, advocatus, causidicus): paterni juris,; cf. : juris et libertatis, id. Rab. perd. 4, 12: octo tribuni plebis, illius adversarii, defensores mei,; cf. ; opp. petitor,: bonus, et saep.; opp. accusator,; ; et saep.; cf. patronus. Once fem.: mulier defensor alicujus,: canes defensores,.—
Esp. in plur., defensores, the garrison: oppidum vacuum ab defensoribus,; et saep.; ; ; ; et saep.—
Defensor civitatis, or plebis, or loci, in the later period of the empire (since 365 A.D.), title of a magistrate in the provincial cities, whose chief duty was to afford protection against oppression on the part of the governor; he was likewise endowed with a subordinate civil jurisdiction,; ; .—*
Of inanimate subjects, as the guards (sublicae) of a bridge,

la:verb:deficio.gloss: to move away, leave, withdraw, break away
senses: to move away, leave, withdraw, break away
to be exhausted, run out, fail, run out, be wanting, fail, cease, disappear, come to nothing, vanish
to be discouraged, disappoint or let down
to be lacking in, to fall short, have shortcomings, fail
la:verb:deficio.html:
dē-fĭcĭo, fēci, fectum, 3 (
perf. subj.: defexit, an old formula in , see below, no. III. fin. In the pass., besides the regular form deficior, ante- and postclass., once in Verg., Propert., and Livy, like fīo, eri: defit, Enn. ap. ; ; ; ; ; : deflunt,: defiat,; : defiet,: defieri,; cf. conficio init.), v. a. and n.
facio
, orig., to loosen, set free, remove from; but it passed over at a very early period into the middle sense, to loosen from one's self, to remove one's self, to break loose from; and then gradually assumed the character of a new verb. act., with the meaning to leave, desert,

depart from something, or absol., to depart, cease, fail. (For syn. cf.: desum, absum, descisco, negligo.)

Act. in the middle sense, to remove one's self, separate one's self, to withdraw (cf. the Greek ἀφιστάναι).—Hence, to forsake, desert, abandon, revolt.
Lit.: ab amicitia P. R.,; : ab Aeduis,: ab rege,; cf. : (consules) a senatu, a republica, a bonis omnibus defecerant,; cf.: a republica,; ; : ab imperio ac nomine nostro, et saep.: a patribus ad plebem,to go over,: ad se,; cf.: ad Poenos,.—Absol.: civitates quae defecerant,; ; —
Trop.: si a virtute defeceris,forsake,: si utilitas ab amicitia defecerit,: ut a me ipse deficerem,.—Hence,
As a verb. act., to leave a person or thing, to desert, to fail, forsake, be wanting to (of things; very rarely of personal subjects): quem jam sanguis viresque deficiunt,; so, vires,; : me Leontina civitas,; fin.; et saep.: res eos jam pridem, fides deficere nuper coepit,: me dies, vox, latera deficiant, si, etc., (imitated word for word, ); cf.: ne te de republica disserentem deficiat oratio,; and: tempus te citius quam oratio deficeret,: animus si te non deficit aequus,: somnus sollicitas domus,: genitor Phaethontis orbem, i. e. is eclipsed (cf. III. B. infra), .—Poet. with a subject-clause: nec me deficiet nautas rogitare citatos, i. e. I will not cease, etc. Kuin.—
Pass.: cum aquilifer jam viribus deficeretur,; cf.: mulier a menstruis defecta,: mulier abundat audacia, consilio et ratione deficitur,: aqua ciboque defecti,; : sanguine defecti artus, et saep.: si qui dotem promisit defectus sit facultatibus,i. e. unable to pay,; cf.: te defecta nomina,—
Middle or neuter, to run out, be wanting, fail, cease, disappear.
Middle (mostly ante-class. and poet.).
With dat.: mihi fortuna magis nunc defit, quam genus, Enn. ap. ; : lac mihi non aestate novum, non frigore defit,.—
Absol.: neque opsonium defiat neque supersit,; so opp. superesse,: ut defiat dies,: : numquamne causa defiet, cur? etc.,.—Trop.: defectis (sc. animo) defensoribus,disheartened,: sed non usque eo defectum Germanicum,weakened,; cf. in the foll. no. B. β.—
Neuter.
With dat. (so rarely; mostly poet.): cum non solum vires, sed etiam tela nostris deficerent,; so perh.: vires nostris, (al. nostros); Oud. N. cr.; cf. ; and .—
Absol. (freq. in all periods and kinds of composition): non frumentum deficere poterat,; cf.: fructus ex arboribus,fin.: ejus generis copia,: tempus anni ad bellum gerendum,: vereor, ne mihi crimina non suppeterent, ne oratio deesset, ne vox viresque deficerent,: nisi memoria forte defecerit,; : non deficiente crumena, et saep.; : quod plena luna defecisset,was eclipsed,; cf.: solem lunae oppositum solere deficere, al.; also simply to set: qua venit exoriens, qua deficit,: lunā deficiente, waning (opp. crescente), ; of fire and light, to go out, expire, become extinct: ignis,: lumen,: progenies Caesarum in Nerone deficit,becomes extinct, dies out,; cf. ; ; ; but deficit ignis,does not extend,: in hac voce defecit,he departed, expired,; prooem. § 11: deficit omne quod nascitur, comes to an end, ; cf.: mundum deficere,: deficit vita,; quod multi Gallicis tot bellis defecerant,had been lost,: ultima jam passi comites bello Deficiunt,grow faint,: deficit Matho,fails, becomes bankrupt,: debitores,: munimenta defecerant,yielded, surrendered,.—Trop.: ne negotio desisteret neu animo deficeret,nor be disheartened,; so, animo,; ; ; ; for which, ne deficiant (apes) animum,; and in a like sense absol.: ne una plaga accepta patres conscripti conciderent, ne deficerent,; so ; : deficit ars,: illis legibus populus Romanus prior non deficiet: si prior defexit publico consilio dolo malo, tu illo die, Juppiter, etc., to depart from, violate the conditions of a treaty, an old formula used in taking an oath, : pugnando deficere,i. e. to be deficient, wanting,; cf. poet. with foll. inf.: suppeditare Materies,; ; .— Hence, dēfectus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to no. III.), weak, weakened, worn out, enfeebled (not ante-Aug.): quod sibi defectis illa tulisset opem,: defectus annis et desertus viribus,; cf.: defectissimus annis et viribus, prooem. § 12: senio (arbor),: laboribus,: vadit incerto pede, jam viribus defecta,: defectae senectutis homine,: in tumidis et globosis (speculis) omnia defectiora (corresp. with paria and auctiora),smaller,.—Plur. subst.: dēfecti, ōrum, m.: sidera obscura attributa defectis,the weak,.

la:verb:deflecto.gloss: to bend or turn downwards or away; to deflect
senses: to bend or turn downwards or away; to deflect
la:verb:deflecto.html:
dē-flecto, xi, xum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act., to bend downwards or aside, to turn aside or in another direction.
Lit.: ramum olivae,; cf.: palmitem,; Catull. 62, 51; : tela (Venus),: amnis in alium cursum,: cursum ad Romanos. : vultum ab aliqua re ad aliquid,: carinam quolibet,; cf.: rapidum iter,; novam viam,to turn off, construct in another direction,—
Trop.
In gen.: lumina,; cf.: oculos a cura,, 76: cum ipsos principes aliqua pravitas de via deflexit,: aliquem ab institutis studiis,: ut declinet a proposito deflectatque sententiam,: si ad verba rem deflectere velimus,: quaedam in senectute deflexit (for which, shortly before, mutavit), Cels. praef.: in ipsos factum deflectitur,: adversarios in suam utilitatem deflectere,; cf.: dotes puellae in pejus,: tragoediam in obscenos risus,: perniciosa consilia fortuna deflexit in melius,: virtutes in vitia,: se de curriculo petitionis,to withdraw,—
Esp. (late Lat.), gramm. t. t., to inflect, to vary the form of a word: non solet sic deflecti,.—
Neutr., to turn off, turn aside.
Lit.: vulgus militum deflectere viā,; cf. without via,: in Tuscos,.—
Trop. (freq., but almost exclusively in Cicero): deflexit jam aliquantulum de spatio curriculoque consuetudo majorum,; so, de via (consuetudo),: de recta regione,: a veritate,: oratio redeat illuc unde deflexit,: a Domino,; .
la:verb:deflecto.inflection: xi, xum, 3, v. a. and n.

senses: to move, float or swim downwards or downstream softly or gradually; flow or stream down; glide down, descend
to flow or pass away, drain off, cease flowing, disappear
to cease, vanish, pass away, disappear; to be lost
la:verb:defluo.html:
dē-flŭo, xi, xum, 3, v. n.
To flow down.
Lit.: quod sanguen defluxerat, Cato ap. ; cf.: sanguis a renibus,: defluit lapidosus rivus,: flamma ex Aetna monte,: flumen Lavida Tauro monte defluens, Fragm. ap. P.; cf.: saxis umor,; : Anaxum quo Varamus defluit,: potus defluit ad pulmonem,.—
Transf., of things not liquid, to move downwards softly or gradually; to glide or flow down, descend: jam ipsae defluebant coronae,.—Of clothing: pedes vestis defluxit ad imos,: toga defluit male laxus,hangs carelessly,.—Of floating objects: aries mersus secundo defluit amni,floats, swims down,; ; : Ostiam Tiberi,to sail down,; —Of riders: tota cohors imitata relictis Ad terram defluxit equis,dismounted,; cf.: ex equo,: in humum (ex equo), Furius poët. ap. : ad terram,; and, a dextro armo in latus,.—
Trop., to flow, come, pass: hoc totum e sophistarum fontibus defluxit in forum,: a necessariis artificiis ad elegantiora,; cf.: (adolescentes) tantum ab eo (sc. Seneca) defluebant, quantum, etc.,departed, deviated, Frotsch., : a quibus duplex Octaviorum familia defluxit,are derived, descended,; cf. : ne quid in terram defluat,be spilled on the ground, be lost,: multaque merces tibi defluat aequo ab Jove,flow to thee in abundance, (cf. Theocr. 1, 5: Ἔς τε καταῤῥεῖ): a superis,; cf.: si quid redundarit, ad illum defluxisse, etc.,. —
To flow or pass away so as to disappear, to cease flowing.
Lit.: rusticus exspectat dum defluat amnis,; cf.: cum hiberni defluxere torrentes,.—
Trop., to cease, vanish, pass away, disappear, be lost: ex novem tribunis unus defluxit,has deserted, proved unfaithful,: ubi salutatio defluxit,has ceased, is over,: ubi per socordiam vires, tempus, ingenium defluxere,: tenerae sucus Defluat praedae,; .—So of the falling out of the hair, ; : comae,.—In eccl. Lat. = defloresco: folium,; ; .

la:verb:defungor.gloss: to have done with, perform, finish, carry out
senses: to have done with, perform, finish, carry out
la:verb:defungor.html:
dē-fungor, functus (
infin. pass. parag. defungier, ), 3, v. dep., to have done with, to acquit one's self of, to discharge an affair or an obligation (esp. an unwelcome, unpleasant one), to perform, finish (class.).
With abl.: aliquo studio,: tam vili munere orationis, Planc. ap. : omni populari concitatione,: periculis,; : tribus decumis pro una,: hoc mendacio, Cael. ap. : imperio regis,: proelio,; cf. bello,: consulis fato,; cf.: fatalibus malis,: plurimorum morbis, perpaucis funeribus,: poena,; : laboribus,; et saep.; esp. of the finishing of this (troublesome) life (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): vitā,to die,; ; : suis temporibus,; but, sua morte,: honesta morte,; : terrā,; cf. the foll. —Poet., with inanimate subjects: defunctum bello barbiton,discharged from the warfare of love,.—
Absol.: nec adversus illos mercede defungor,nor do I discharge my obligation by the payment,: defunctus jam sum, now I am quit, i. e. safe, out of danger, Ruhnk.; cf. ; ; .—To depart, die (not ante Aug.; cf. supra): dicitur prius esse defunctus,; ; : honesta morte,; hence, defunctus, = mortuus,deceased, defunct,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; . 18.—Plur.: defuncti, m., the dead, Sen. ad. Marc. 13, 2; ; ; ; et saep.

la:verb:defetiscor.gloss: to become tired, grow weary, be exhausted
senses: to become tired, grow weary, be exhausted
la:verb:defetiscor.html:
dē-fĕtiscor (in MSS. sometimes defatiscor), fessus, 3,
v. dep. n., to become tired or wearied; to grow weary, faint; to be exhausted. (For syn. v. defatigo. As a verb. fin. ante-class. and rare, but class. and freq. in the part. perf.): neque defetiscar experirier,; so with inf.: ego sum defessus reperire, vos defessi quaerere, (for which, sum defessus quaeritando, ); ; ; : non si quid malae pugnae acciderit, defetiscendum, Front. B. Parth.: ego vapulando, ille verberando usque ambo defessi sumus,; so, defessus with abl. gerund., ; ; Afran. ap. ; ; cf.: aggerunda aqua defessi,.—With abl. nominis: diuturnitate pugnae defessi,; cf. the foll.: defessus totius diei labore,; cf. : vulneribus,: cultu agrorum,: forensibus negotiis atque urbano opere,; fin.: convicio (aures), et saep.: semperque ipsi recentes defessis succederent,; so opp. recens or integer, ; ; ; : defessi Aeneadae,; cf. ; : defessus omnibus medullis, Catul. 55, 30; .—
Transf., of things: arbores defatiscentes,: ita defessa ac refrigerata accusatio,weakened,; cf. oratio,: orant defessis subeant rebus, i. e. afflictis,.

la:verb:defleo.gloss: to weep over, cry for, lament, deplore
senses: to weep over, cry for, lament, deplore
to weep abundantly or violently, weep to exhaustion
la:verb:defleo.html:
dē-flĕo, ēvi, ētum, 2, v. a. and n.
Act.
To weep over a person or thing; to lament, deplore, bewail (for syn. cf.: deploro, ejulo, ploro, lacrimo, lamentor, fleo —class.): te cinefactum deflevimus,: Numam,: nuptam (Eurydicen),: inter nos impendentes casus deflevimus,: illud initium civilis belli, Asinius Pollio ap. : eversionem civitatis,: aliena mala, et saep.: Crassi mors a multis saepe defleta,; cf. ; : in deflenda nece, et saep. —Absol.: dum assident, dum deflent,: in amici sinu,.—
Poet. with acc. and inf.: et minui deflevit onus dorsumque levari,.—*
Oculos, to dull with weeping, .—
Neutr., to weep much or violently, weep to exhaustion (very rare): gravibus cogor deflere querelis,; Justin. 18, 4, 13;
la:verb:defleo.inflection: ēvi, ētum, 2, v. a. and n.

la:verb:defodio.gloss: to dig deep or downwards; excavate
senses: to dig deep or downwards; excavate
la:verb:defodio.html:
dē-fŏdĭo, fōdi, fossum, 3, v. a.
To dig downwards or deep; to dig up, to dig (rare): scrobem in limine stabuli,: specus,: domos,: terram,: locum in altitudinem pedum quinque,: defosso lacu,.—More freq.,
To bury in the earth (quite class.): homines defoderunt in terram dimidiatos, Cato ap. ; ; ; : thesaurum defossum esse sub lecto,; cf. : cotem et novaculam in comitio,: hospitem (necatum) in aedibus,; : lapidem in agro,: aliquem humo,; .—
Transf., to hide,

conceal, cover: defodiet (aetas) condetque nitentia,: quae necessitas hominem defodit, ut erueret aurum,; : se,

la:adj:deformis.gloss: Departing physically from the correct shape; deformed, ugly, misshapen, malformed.
senses: Departing physically from the correct shape; deformed, ugly, misshapen, malformed.
Departing morally from the correct quality; unbecoming; shameful, disgraceful, base.
la:adj:deformis.html:
dē-formis, e (
abl. plur.: deformīs dentibus, Apul. Met. 10, p. 249, 9), adj.
forma; cf. 2. deformo
.
Departing, either physically or (more freq.) morally, from the right shape, quality, etc.; misshapen, deformed, unsightly, ugly, odious, disgusting; disgraceful, base (for syn. cf.: taeter, foedus, turpis—freq. and class.): longus an brevis, formosus an deformis,: deformem esse natum,; cf.: calvitio quoque deformis,; and, deformissima femina (opp. pulcherrima),: opus non deforme,: nec ulla deformior species est civitatis quam, etc.,; cf. patria,: solum patriae belli malis,; cf. : agmen (sc. inerme),: turba,; cf. : spectaculum,; ; cf. aspectus (opp. species honesta),: motus statusve, et saep.: oratio non tam honorifica audientibus quam sibi deformis,; cf. : blanditiae,: convicia,: libido,: haesitatio,: obsequium,servile,: aegrimonia, et saep.: deforme et servile est caedi discentes,; so with a subject-clause, (opp. foedissimum); and 125; al.; and in the comp., ; fin.; .—N. plur. as subst.: deformia meditari,shameful deeds,.—* Poet. with gen.: deformis leti,.—Adv. (post-Aug.): dēformĭ-ter.
Misshapenly: formati, Apul. M. 8, p. 214, 4.—
Inelegantly; disgracefully: sonat junctura,: dicet multa,: vivo,.—Comp.: deformius errasse, Sulpic. Sev. Dial. 1, 6, 6. —*
Shapeless: animae,.

senses: failing, failure, deficiency, want, disappearance, decline
a fainting spell, failure of energy or stamina
la:noun:defectio.html:
dēfectĭo, ōnis, f.
deficio
.
Defection, desertion, rebellion, revolt.
Lit.: rebellio facta post deditionem, defectio datis obsidibus,; ; ; ; : Ampsivariorum a tergo, in the rear (of Caesar), ; et saep.: subita defectio Pompeii,: imperii,from the empire,.—*
Trop.: intemperantia, quae est a tota mente et a recta ratione defectio,.—
(Acc. to deficio, no. III.) A failing, failure, deficiency, want, disappearance.
Lit. (so most freq.): ista ipsa defectio virium adolescentiae vitiis efficitur saepius quam senectutis,: aquarum, 91: pecuniae,: rerum,.—
Esp. of the obscuration of the heavenly bodies, an eclipse: solis defectiones itemque lunae praedicuntur in multos annos,; fin.; ; ; ; ; et saep.—
Also (sc. virium), exhaustion, faintness, swooning, fainting (post-Aug. prose), , praef. § 4: animae,a swoon,; : alvo usque ad defectionem soluta,; cf. : recreandae defectioni cibum adferre, (50); cf.: defectione perire, by exhaustion, i. e. by disease, : in cunctis renibus,.—
In the later grammarians, an ellipsis: dicere aliquid per defectionem,by ellipsis, elliptically,; ; — *
Trop.: Quintus frater omnia mittit spei plena, metuens credo defectionem animi mei,my want of courage, despondency,.

la:verb:defigo.gloss: to stick, thrust, or plunge (a weapon)
senses: to stick, thrust, or plunge (a weapon)
to bewitch or enchant (by sticking pins in a model)
la:verb:defigo.html:
dē-fīgo, xi, xum, 3,
v. a., to fasten down or in; and with especial reference to the terminus, to drive, fix, or fasten into (class.). —
Lit.: in campo Martio crucem ad civium supplicium defigi et constitui jubes, Cic. Rab. perd. 4; so, tigna machinationibus immissa in flumen,: sudes sub aqua,: asseres in terra defigebantur,; : verutum in balteo,: sicam in consulis corpore,to thrust,; cf.: cultrum in corde,: tellure hastas,; cf. : gladium superne jugulo,; cf. : cruci defiguntur, Varr. ap. : arborem penitus terrae,: te hodie, si prehendero, defigam in terram colaphis, (for which, shortly after, cruci affigere): morsus in aurem,: clavum percussum malleo in cerebrum,; Eccles. 12, 11. —
Meton. (Causa pro effectu.) To fix, fasten, render immovable (rare): defixa caelo sidera,; cf. : defixere aciem in his vestigiis,have fixed them motionless,; cf.: defixi et Neronem intuentes,: sedeo defixus,: me defixum in ora, etc.,.—
Esp. in phrase, manus defigere, to strike hands, i. e., to close a contract as surety, to pledge one's person, ; .—
Trop.
In gen., to fix, fasten; to turn intently in any direction: virtus est una altissimis defixa radicibus,: oculos in vultu regis,: iratos oculos in te,: in alicujus possessiones oculos defigere,: oculos defigere in terram,; .—Absol.: oculos,to let fall, cast down,: Aeneas defixus lumina,: animos in ea, quae perspicua sunt,: disputare non vaganti oratione, sed defixa in una republica,; cf.: in eo mentem orationemque defigit,: omnes suas curas in reip. salute,; ; cf. .—
In partic.
To strike motionless, sc. with astonishment, etc.; to stupefy, astound, astonish (not freq. till after the Aug. per.): utraque simul objecta res oculis animisque immobiles parumper eos defixit,; so, aliquem,; : silentium triste ita defixit omnium animos, ut, etc., .—In the part. perf.: dum stupet obtutuque haeret defixus in uno,; ; ; ; ; ; et saep.—
Religious t. t. *
To declare fixedly, firmly, unalterably: QVAE AVGVR VITIOSA, DIRA DEFIXERIT, IRRITA SVNTO,—
(Because, in making imprecations, the waxen image of him for whom destruction was to be prepared, or his name written in wax, was stuck through with a needle; cf. , and Voss upon .) To bewitch, enchant; to curse any thing: caput alicujus dira imprecatione,: defigi imprecationibus,: nomina cerā,; cf.: DEFIXA NOMINA,: regis animum Iolchiacis votis,.—
To censure, reprove a thing: culpam,.

la:verb:defunctus.gloss: done with, performed, finished, having finished
senses: done with, performed, finished, having finished

la:verb:deformo.gloss: to form, fashion; to design, delineate, describe
senses: to form, fashion; to design, delineate, describe
to deform, disfigure; to spoil, mar
la:verb:deformo.html:
dē-formo, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to bring into form or shape; to form, fashion; to design, delineate, describe (class.).
Lit.: areas,; : marmora prima manu,: non flosculos sed certos ac deformatos fructus ostenderat,full-formed, perfect,: tragicae (scenae) deformantur columnis et fastigiis et signis,are delineated, represented,; cf.: operis speciem exemplaribus pictis,to represent in outline, to sketch,.—
Trop.: quae ita a fortuna deformata sunt, ut tamen a natura inchoata compareant,; cf. : ille, quem supra deformavi,have depicted, described,; : ministratio deformata litteris,.

la:verb:defringo.html:
dē-fringo, frēgi, fractum, 3,
v. a., to break off; to break to pieces (rare but class.).
Lit.: amphoram defracto collo puram impleto,: plantas,; cf. : ramum arboris,: surculum,: ferrum summā ab hasta,: crura aut cervices sibi,; so, lumbos,: caput ei testatim, Juventius ap. P.; cf.: caput ei hoc patibulo, Titin. ap. .—
Trop.: id unum bonum est, quod numquam defringitur,is never destroyed,; Apul. .

la:verb:defendo#2.html:
dē-fendo, di, sum (
infin. pass. parag.: defendier, : .— Part. gen. plur. sync.: defendentum,), 3, v. a.
arch.: FENDO; cf. Sanscr. han (ghan), to smite; Gr. θείνω; hence, also offendo, infensus, infestus, mani-festus; cf. fustis
, to fend or ward off any thing hostile or injurious; to repel, avert, keep off: propulsando arcere (for syn. cf.: tueor, tutor, servo, conservo. propugno, protego, vindico, caveo—freq. and class.); regularly constr. with acc. alone (so in Cic. and Caes.); very rarely aliquid (aliquem) ab aliquo, and in poets also aliquid alicui; cf. Zumpt. Gr. § 469.
Aliquid (aliquem): ut tu morbos calamitates intemperiasque prohibessis, defendas averruncesque,: serva cives, defende hostes, cum potes defendere, Enn. ap. ; cf. bellum (opp. inferre),; fin.: ad defendendos ictus ac repellendos,; cf.: ignis jactus et lapides,: frigus et solem,; cf.: nimios solis ardores,; and frigus,; also: sitim fonte et purā lymphā,to quench,: qui non defendit injuriam neque propulsat,; so, injuriam,: noxiam,: imperatoris sui tribunorumque plebis injurias,: vim suorum,; cf.: vim illatam vi,: pericula,; : hunc furorem,: dedecus manu, et saep.: crimen,to answer, defend against an accusation,.—
With ab: (milites) a pinnis hostes defendebant facillime, Quadrig. ap. ; cf. : hostem a fossa,: ignem a tectis,.—
Aliquid alicui (cf. arceo, no. II. d.): iniuriam foribus,: solstitium pecori,; cf.: aestatem capellis,; : tela misero,: dedecus morti,: senium famae,.—
Absol., to put a stop (to a fire), to check the flames: nec quisquam defendere audebat, crebris minis restinguere prohibentium,; cf.: urbem incendere, feris in populum immissis, quo difficilius defenderentur,.—
Transf., like prohibere, with acc. of that from which any thing is warded off or averted, to defend, guard, protect, cover.
In gen. (so most freq. in all perr. and species of composition), constr. with acc. alone; with acc. and ab aliquo (contra aliquid), or merely ab aliquo; and absol.
With simple acc.: Aeduos ceterosque amicos populi Rom.,: eos,; : se armis,: se manu,; 6, 40, 6 et saep.: castra,fin.; ; (with tueri): oppidum, et saep.: eum defendo, quem tu accusas,: aliquem apud praetores,: aliquem de ambitu,: cf. causam,; ; et passim: d. ac tegere scelus,; cf. with protegere,: justitiam,: communem salutem,; et saep.: locum,to preserve, maintain,; cf.: vicem modo rhetoris atque poëtae,to sustain,: actorum partes,: aedes Vestae vix defensa est (sc. ab incendio),preserved,.—
Aliquid (aliquem) ab aliquo: Aedui cum se suaque ab iis defendere non possent,: se a finitimis,; ; et saep.: Galliam omnem ab Ariovisti injuria,; so, aliquem ab injuria,; ; cf. : se regnumque suum ab Romanorum avaritia,: provinciam non modo a calamitate, sed etiam a metu calamitatis,: Italiam a vastatione, Planc. ap. : vitam ab inimicorum audacia telisque,: libertatis causam ab regio praesidio, et saep.: teneras myrtos a frigore,: frondes ab acutae vulnere falcis, a pecoris morsu, et saep.—
With ab aliquo: quod et ab incendio lapis et ab ariete materia defendit,; so ; .—
Aliquem (aliquid) contra, or adversus aliquem: me scio a te contra iniquos meos solere defendi,: sese adversus populum Romanum defendere,: me adversus Abrupolim,; ; ; : auctoritatem contra invidiam,; ; ; ; ; ; .—(ε) Absol.: filii qui et sentire et defendere possent,: cum jam defenderet nemo,: defendentibus civibus Romanis,; cf. in the abl. absol., ; ; et saep.: quibus eae partes ad defendendum obvenerunt, —
In partic.
Of speech, to defend, support, maintain; to bring forward, allege in defence (so repeatedly in Cic.; elsewhere rare).
With acc.: (Carneades) nullam umquam in illis suis disputationibus rem defendit, quam non probarit,; cf. : me id maxime defendisse, ut, etc.,have chiefly striven for,; ; .—
With acc. and inf.: gravissimeque et verissime defenditur, numquam aequitatem ab utilitate posse sejungi, etc.,; ; : ille nihil ex his sponte susceptum sed principi paruisse defendebat,: sed id solitum esse fieri defendebat,; so with verb pass. and inf., —
With a relative clause: (quae turpitudines) cur non cadant in sapientem, non est facile defendere,. —
In the later jurid. Lat., to claim, vindicate, or prosecute at law: quia libertatem et hereditatem ex testamento sibi defendebat,: si patris mortem defendere necesse habuerit,i. e. legally to avenge his death,; .

la:noun:defectus.html:
dēfectus, ūs, m.
deficio
.
(For defectio, no. I.) Defection, revolt: magno animo defectum eorum tulit, Mützell.: legionum,.—
( = defectio, no. III.) A failing, failure, lack, disappearance (freq. in the elder Pliny; elsewhere rare): lactis (mammae),: stomachi,weakness,: animi,a swoon,: albicante purpurae defectu,fading away into white,: in tanto defectu rerum,freedom from occupation,. Of the eclipsing of the heavenly bodies: solis,; imitated by : ejus (sc. lunae) species ac forma mutatur tum crescendo, tum defectibus in initia recurrendo,

la:noun:definitio.html:
dēfīnītĭo, ōnis, f.
definio
. *
A bounding, a boundary: AREA INTRA HANC DEFINITIONEM CIPPORVM CLAVSA VERVBVS,.—
A limiting, prescribing, defining; a definition, explanation (freq. only in Cicero; cf. definio): ut quodcumque accidisset praedictum videretur hominum et temporum definitione sublata,: judiciorum aequorum,: definitio est earum rerum, quae sunt ejus rei propriae, quam definire volumus, brevis et circumscripta quaedam explicatio, ; cf. ; ; et saep.; : definitio pars sit translationis, et saep.—
Transf., that which is decreed, decided: perpetrata quippe est definitio,.

la:adv:deformiter.html:
dēformĭter,
adv., inelegantly, disgracefully, etc.; v. deformis, no. I. fin.

la:verb:defio.gloss: to move away, leave, withdraw, break away

senses: Of names, those that are missing from certain cases.
la:adj:defectivus.html:
dēfectīvus, a, um, adj. [deficio,
no. III.), imperfect, defective (post-class.): et abortiva genitura,: febris,intermittent fever,.—
In gramm.: nomina, verba, some of whose forms are wanting,defective,.

la:verb:defensito.html:
dēfensĭto, āvi, 1,
v. a. freq. [defenso], to defend often, to practise defending (perh, only in the foll. passages): haec non acrius accusavit in senectute, quam antea defensitaverat,; cf. : causas,;

la:adj:defluus.html:
dēflŭus, a, um, adj.
defluo
,
flowing down; or transf., moving downwards, going or falling down (post-Aug.).
In gen.: gradus,: caesaries, long and flowing, Prud. στεφ. 13, 30: splendor ab alto,.—
Esp.: vasculum (in which a liquid runs down),a water-clock,.

senses: to lose heart or be discouraged
la:verb:defatigo.html:
dē-fătīgo or dē-fĕtīgo, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. a., to weary out, tire a person; to fatigue; to exhaust. (For syn. cf.: fatigo, fessus, lassus, langueo, languidus, defessus. —Freq. and class.)
Lit.
Act.: cum crebro integri defessis succederent nostrosque assiduo labore defatigarent,; cf.: exercitum Pompeii quotidianis itineribus,; et saep.: se,; .—
Pass.: opus faciam ut defatiger usque, ingratiis ut dormiam,: defatigatus vulneribus, Cato

ap. : defatigatus,; and opp. integer,fin.; 7, 85, 7; : defatigatus est populus nimis,.—*

Transf.: ubertate nimia prioris aevi defatigatum et effetum solum,exhausted,, praef. § 1.—
Trop.
Act.: deos suppliciis, votis, precibus, etc., Afran. ap. : ne te adolescens mulier defatiget,: censores, judices,—
Pass.: te nec animi neque corporis laboribus defatigari,; ; : numquam conquiescam neque defatigabor ante, quam, etc.,; cf. .—Once with inf.: nec defatigabor permanere in studio libertatis, Lentulus ap.

la:verb:defervesco.html:
dē-fervesco, fervi and ferbui (defervi, ; ; ; ; :
deferbui,; ; et saep.), 3, v. n. (post-Aug.), to cease boiling, leave off raging.
Lit.: ubi lupinus deferverit,: aestus,: dum musteus fructus defervescat,; cf.: deferbuit mustum,; : ubi caelum enituit et deferbuit mare,.—
Trop.
Of the fire of passion, to cease raging, to cool down, to be allayed, assuaged (a favorite expression of Cic.; elsewh. rare): ut ulciscendi vim differant in tempus aliud, dum defervescat ira: defervescere autem certe significat ardorem animi invita ratione excitatum,: sperabam jam defervisse adolescentiam,; cf.: cum adolescentiae cupiditates defervissent,; : quasi deferverat oratio,: hominum studia defervisse,: dum defervescat haec gratulatio,; : regis indignatio deferbuerat,.—
(Fig. from the fermenting of wine.) To become clarified, clear: novi versiculi ut primum videbuntur defervisse,

la:verb:defugio.html:
dē-fŭgĭo, fūgi, 3, v. a. and n.
Act.
With acc., to run away from; to flee, shun, avoid: fugiendo devitare (class.): aditum alicujus sermonemque,: proelium,: patriam, (dub.): munus,; : injurias fortunae defugiendo relinquas,: eam disputationem,: contentiones, inimicitias, vitae dimicationes,: auctoritatem,to withdraw from responsibility,; ; et saep. —
With quin and subj.: nec tamen defugio quin dicam quae scio,.—
Absol., to shun, avoid, escape: rempublicam suscipiant: sin timore defugiant, etc.,.—
Intrans., to escape by flight, run away: circa ripam Tiberis, quo sinistrum cornu defugit,.

la:noun:defatigatio.html:
dēfătīgātĭo or defĕt-, ōnis, f.
defatigo
.
Act., a wearying, tiring out, fatiguing, ; ; ; .—
Pass., weariness, fatigue, exhaustion, ; ; ;

la:verb:deflagro.html:
dēflā^gro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
To burn down, to be consumed by fire (freq. only in Cic.; cf. conflagro).
Neutr.
Lit.: qua nocte natus esset Alexander, eadem Dianae Ephesiae templum deflagravisse,; ; ; ; ; ; ; : Phaëthon ictu fulminis deflagravit,.—
Trop., to perish, be destroyed: communi incendio malint quam suo deflagrare,: ruere ac deflagrare omnia passuri estis?.—
Act. (very rare): fana flammā deflagrata, Enn. ap. : quae (sol) proxime currendo deflagrat,.—*
Trop., to destroy utterly: in cinere deflagrati imperii, (cf. deflagratio fin.).—
To burn out, cease burning; rare, and only trop. of the fire of passion, = defervesco, to abate, be allayed: deflagrare iras vestras posse,: deflagrante paullatim seditione,: iram senis deflagrare pati,.—Transf. to persons: sic deflagrare minaces Incassum,.
la:verb:deflagro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:noun:deflagratio.html:
dēflā^grātĭo, ōnis, f.
deflagro
,
a burning up, consuming by fire, conflagration (perhaps only in Cic.).
Prop.: futura aliquando caeli atque terrarum,; cf.: terrarum omnium,—
Trop., destruction,

la:verb:defundo.html:
dē-fundo, fūdi, fūsum, 3,
